title: Daniil Medvedev Rises To No. 6 In Race To Turin After Strong Run In Asia
text:

 Daniil Medvedev has climbed to No. 6 in the ATP Race to Turin with 3,420 points after strong performances in Hangzhou and Beijing, bringing him closer to Nitto ATP Finals qualification.
 by Anushka Raghav | Oct 20, 2026 | 2 minute read Daniil Medvedev moved up two places to No. 6 in the ATP Finals race after a strong Asian swing and said his priority remains improving his game rather than focusing on rankings. · Credits; Via ATP Tennis Daniil Medvedev has moved up two places to number six in the PIF ATP race to Turin after playing well in the recent weeks. He is now at 3,420 and he is getting so closer to qualifying for the Nitto ATP Finals, where the top players of the season compete. However, Medvedev said that he wants to focus on playing well rather than worrying too much about his current ranking.
 Medvedev Focuses on Improving His Tennis
 Medvedev feels that his game has improved over the past weeks, especially during the tournament in Hangzhou and Beijing. He said the conditions in Hangzhou reminded him of his earlier years when he played competitively faster on courts, and the way the ball moves through the air can help his serve. They also allow him to hit more aces and put more pressure on his opponent.
 “100% I played really, really well,” Medvedev said about his recent form.
 Medvedev also talked about his match against Novak Djokovic, where he praised his performance and said both the players played at a very high level. Medvedev enjoyed the match throughout and feels that his game is getting better. Now he wants to keep this form going and get more wins in his next tournament.
 “Definitely trying to maintain my level from Hungary and Beijing,” he explained. “When I play like I play there, I can beat a lot of guys, I can win tournaments, and I can make good results.”
 ATP Finals Race Is a Bonus for Medvedev
 Medvedev's rise to No. 6 has strengthened his position in the race for Turin, but he does not see qualification as his main goal. He believes reaching the season-ending event is a reward for having a successful year rather than something players should chase separately.
 “To be there means that you made a good year. So, that's why it's important,” he said.
The Russian admitted that he sometimes checks the rankings but does not want to spend too much time calculating his chances. With several players close together in the standings, the race can change quickly after a single tournament.
 For Medvedev, the main thing is to keep playing well at each game. If he can continue at this level, he will have better chances of making it back to the ATP finals.
